html:
Islam first reached India by sea, with Arab traders on the Malabar coast of Kerala, within a century of the Prophet's death. This was centuries before any Muslim army came through the northwest passes.

Arab ships had sailed to Malabar for pepper since before Roman times (see Muziris). When Arabia turned to Islam in the 7th century, the same merchants brought the faith with them. Many stayed for the season, married local women and raised families. Their descendants are the Mappilas, the oldest Muslim community in South Asia.

A legend says the last Chera king, Cheraman Perumal, saw the moon split, sailed to Mecca and became a Muslim, and that his companions came back and built mosques. The Cheraman Juma Mosque at Kodungallur claims the year 629. Firm evidence begins in the 9th century: a copper-plate grant of 849 at Kollam has Muslim witnesses signing in Arabic script.

The Hindu rulers of the coast, above all the Zamorin of Calicut, protected the Muslim traders and grew rich with them. When the Portuguese tried to seize the pepper trade after 1498, Mappila sailors led by the Kunjali Marakkars fought them at sea for a hundred years.
sum: Islam first reached India by sea, with Arab traders on the Malabar coast of Kerala, within a century of the Prophet's death. This was centuries before any Muslim army came through the northwest passes.
